column1: # Pinned dev toolchain, rows left after the move to mise, read by scripts/tools.sh (make tools).
# Columns (tab-separated): name  version  platform  url  sha256
# Most tools are in mise.toml and mise.lock (mise install --locked, a sha256 per platform for linux-x64 and macos-arm64,
# plus a signature or attestation where the vendor publishes one): Node, uv, Helm 3 and 4, both kubectls, kind,
# kubeconform, promtool, ct, helm-unittest, actionlint, hadolint, gitleaks, squawk, oasdiff, cosign, kyverno, yq,
# bats, shellcheck, lychee. Renovate moves those; `make pins-refresh` re-locks them. What stays here is what mise
# cannot verify as well as today or does not manage: mise itself (the bootstrap), Python and the uv tools (hash-pinned
# requirements), and two data files.
# Rule: a pin is the newest stable release published at least 7 days before it was pinned
# (Renovate minimumReleaseAge). Pinned on 2026-11-20.
# mise: the tool manager that installs the rest. Its sha256 is the release's SHASUMS256.txt. The
# release also ships SHASUMS256.txt.minisig (minisign) and SHASUMS256.asc (OpenPGP); neither is checked here, because
# checking either needs a minisign or gpg binary that the toolchain does not have before it has installed mise.
# The mise row is first and is installed first; .tools/bin/mise runs with the repo-local settings in mise.toml (see scripts/tools.sh).
mise
mise
# Rows with url uv:<pkg> are Python tools. Each is installed into its own venv,
# .tools/uv-tools/<name>, with `uv pip install --require-hashes -r tools/requirements/<name>.txt`
# (every transitive dependency hash-pinned; `make pins-refresh` regenerates a lock in place with
# `uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-header --python-version 3.13 --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
# plus `--exclude-newer` (now minus 7 days) and pyyaml held at the version in tools/requirements/pyyaml.txt),
# on the pinned `python` row. mise's pipx backend does not hash-pin transitive dependencies, so these stay.
# Their sha256 column is `-` because the hashes live in the requirements file. yamale and yamllint
# are what `ct lint` shells out to. `uv:python` runs `uv python install <version>` (uv's own download, kept under
# .tools/uv); uv verifies that download with its built-in checksums, which is accepted here.
# The pinned uv itself is in mise.toml; the backend image copies it from the official image at the same version (a test keeps the two equal).
# Helm major: see the default-helm line. Both majors are installed (helm3, helm4, in mise.toml); `helm` links to the default.
#default-helm: 4
# Reason: with Helm 4.3.2 and 3.22.1 against the chart and no cluster, `helm lint`,
# `helm template | kubeconform -strict` (33 resources valid) and `helm unittest` pass on both majors,
# `ct lint` (before the values files were reformatted) exited 1 on both with byte-identical output, because of
# yamllint "braces" findings in the chart's values.yaml (a chart issue, not a Helm-major difference); it passes now. Helm 4 is the current line (and what the owner's
# machine runs), so the template targets it; helm3 stays installed to prove the chart still renders
# on 3.x. The helm3 pin only has to render the chart.
# k8s-openapi is data, not a tool: the Kubernetes OpenAPI spec at a release tag, which
# scripts/ci/kubeconform.sh turns into the JSON schemas it validates against, offline. Its version is
# the chart's kubeVersion floor (Chart.yaml), newest patch of that minor; move it with the floor. No
# vendor checksum exists: hashed on download, and a changed file is refused.
# kyverno-chart is data, not a tool: the Helm chart of the Kyverno release matching the CLI in mise.toml, which
# tests/k8s/test_admission.py installs on kind (chart 3.10 is Kyverno 1.20; move the two together). Its sha256 is the
# digest the chart repository's index.yaml lists, confirmed against the downloaded bytes; hashed on download.
k8s-openapi
kyverno-chart
python
zizmor
schemathesis
pre-commit
yamale
